title: $100k Net Worth
difficulty: The Hardest First Milestone (Charlie Munger Principle)
description: Reaching your first $100,000 is universally considered the most difficult financial hurdle because nearly 100% of it comes from pure savings discipline before compound interest takes over.

agePercentiles.context: At age 25, having $100,000 net worth puts you far ahead of the vast majority of peers, most of whom are paying down student loans.
By age 30, $100k places you comfortably in the top third of American households.
At age 35, $100k is slightly below the national median ($135,600) as home equity and retirement balances accelerate.
By age 40, median US household net worth exceeds $175,000, making $100k an indicator of delayed retirement savings.
At age 50, median US net worth is $247,200. Catch-up contributions are recommended.

title: $250k Net Worth (Quarter Million)
description: At $250k, annual investment returns at 8% generate $20,000/year passively, equaling a significant portion of average annual living expenses.

agePercentiles.context: A quarter-million at 25 represents early tech equity, business ownership, or exceptional early career income.
At 30, $250,000 places you in the top 16% of all American households in your age group.
At 35, $250k puts you well above the median ($135k) and in the upper third.
At 40, $250k keeps you ahead of average households.
At 50, $250k is right around the national median ($247,200).

title: $500k Net Worth (Half Million)
difficulty: Coast FIRE & Real Financial Independence Foundation
description: At half a million dollars, 7-8% market returns generate $35,000–$40,000 annually without touching the principal. For many, this marks Coast FIRE status.

agePercentiles.context: Extremely rare at age 25, representing early high-growth startups or significant inheritances/investments.
At 30, $500k net worth puts you in the top 7% nationally.
At 35, a half-million dollars places you firmly in the top fifth of households.
At 40, you are comfortably ahead of roughly 3 out of 4 American households.
At 50, $500k provides a resilient foundation for traditional retirement planning.

title: $1 Million Net Worth (Millionaire Status)
description: Achieving seven figures remains the gold standard of financial security, placing a household in the top tier across every demographic age bracket.

agePercentiles.context: Fewer than 1 in 200 people under 25 have attained seven-figure net worth.
Reaching $1,000,000 by 30 is an extraordinary achievement, putting you ahead of 97% of your peers.
At 35, a million-dollar net worth secures your position in the top 9% of US households.
At 40, $1M places you well inside the top 16% of Americans.
By age 50, approximately 1 in 4 US households achieves $1M net worth when including home equity.

title: $2 Million Net Worth (Multi-Millionaire)
description: Under the standard 4% safe withdrawal rule, $2,000,000 provides $80,000/year in passive perpetual income adjusted for inflation, qualifying as full financial independence.

agePercentiles.context: Near top 0.1% in the nation for this age bracket.
At 30, $2M places you firmly within the top 1% of young Americans.
At 35, you rank above 96% of all American households.
At 40, $2M puts you in the top decile (top 9%) nationally.
At 50, $2M provides rock-solid retirement safety well ahead of the national curve.
